faq.question: What is a simple operation and what is an advanced operation?
faq.answer: Simple operations are reads: downloading an object, reading its metadata with a HEAD, and the bucket-level GETs. Advanced operations are everything else: uploads, copies, renames, and listing a bucket. The rate is the same whether a read is served from the origin or from the CDN. Deletes are free.

faq.question: Which region should I choose for my bucket?
faq.answer: None. There is no region to choose. A bucket is global: every file is replicated to a CDN worldwide, so a reader in Singapore and a reader in Frankfurt are both served from close by without you configuring anything. This also means one rate sheet instead of per-region pricing, and no charge for replication or cross-region transfer.

faq.question: Is a failed request billed?
faq.answer: Usually yes. A request that fails on the caller's side is still counted as an operation and billed at the same rate as a successful one: 404 Not Found, 412 Precondition Failed, 400 Bad Digest, and a 403 Access Denied raised after the credentials checked out. Throttling responses, 429 and 503, are billed the same way. Two things are free: a request rejected before authentication with 401 Unauthorized, and any request that fails on our side with a 5xx.

faq.question: How is storage measured?
faq.answer: On the monthly average of your bucket's size, not on its peak. We sample daily and divide by the number of days in the month, so an object stored for one day of a 30-day month costs about a thirtieth of a full month.

faq.question: When am I charged for bandwidth?
faq.answer: Only on bytes that leave the bucket. Uploads are free, so writing an object costs storage and one advanced operation but no bandwidth. Downloads are billed at the same rate whether they are served from the CDN cache or from the origin.

faq.question: How is usage rounded?
faq.answer: Up, to the next whole billing unit, on every meter. 1.1 GB of storage is billed as 2 GB, 1.1 GB of bandwidth as 2 GB, and 1,000,001 simple operations as 2M. The rounding applies once to each meter's total for the month, not to every request.

faq.question: What happens if I exceed the free tier?
faq.answer: Your bucket stops serving requests until the 30-day window rolls over. You are never charged on the free plan. Adding a credit card upgrades you to pay-as-you-go, which removes the caps and bills your usage from the first unit.

faq.question: Does the pay-as-you-go plan include a free allowance?
faq.answer: No. The monthly allowance belongs to the free plan only. On pay-as-you-go you are billed from the first byte stored and the first operation made, at $0.02 per GB of storage, $0.02 per GB of outbound bandwidth, $0.30 per 1M simple operations and $4.50 per 1M advanced operations.

faq.question: Is Upstash Blob S3 compatible?
faq.answer: Yes. Your bucket token exchanges for temporary S3 credentials, so you can use the AWS SDK, the AWS CLI, or any S3-compatible tool alongside the @upstash/blob SDK.

faq.question: What is the maximum file size?
faq.answer: 5 TB per object. For files over 100 MB we recommend multipart uploads, where each part counts as a separate advanced operation.

faq.question: Can I serve files publicly?
faq.answer: Yes. A public bucket gets its own URL and anyone with a link can read from it; writes still require credentials. Private buckets have no public URL and every read must be signed.
